newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong charity sends N.Korea 10 tonnes food aid.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong charity sends N.Korea 10 tonnes food aid.

text.p: A non-profit charity group in Hong Kong said on Friday it was sending 10 tonnes of food and medical aid to famine-ravaged North Korea.
World Vision's Hong Kong office said the HK$1.3 million (US$168,000) worth of assistance would be given to 12 orphanages in Stalinist-ruled North Korea, which has been suffering from severe drought.
A spokeswoman from the international charity body said the aid would arrive in Pyongyang from Beijing next Friday as there was no direct flight from Hong Kong to the North Korean capital.
The spokeswoman said World Vision would also send a group of observers to assess the famine situation in North Korea.
International aid agencies have stepped up food appeals for the Stalinist state, warning of imminent starvation, particularly among young children who are most at risk.
The United Nations food aid agency on Thursday appealed to Western countries to give more aid to North Korea to meet a shortfall of up to 800,000 tonnes of food.
